root_idea.summary: The root's primary concrete referent is the human finger or digit.
root_idea.development: From the concrete finger, the lexicon extends to pointing and indication, controlled manipulation with the fingers, and metaphorical notions of a visible impress or influence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular dictionary citation form إِصْبَعٌ rather than the Quranic plural lemma أَصَٰبِع.

senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrences use the plural form أَصَابِعَ, referring specifically to fingers. The term denotes the digit as a whole, including its constituent parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To point at or toward someone or something with the finger, whether disparagingly or as a means of indicating or directing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported use involves pointing disparagingly or intending harm while the other person is unaware; the same pointing construction is also used to direct someone toward a person, road, or hidden thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To insert one's finger into something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of putting a finger into offered food and of probing a hen to determine whether she is near laying an egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To channel or let liquid flow between the fingers into a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The fingers are used to control the stream so that the liquid does not scatter or pour forth too freely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hit or hurt someone's finger.
To come forth upon a people or party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is reported as possibly originating in صَبَأَ, with hamza, rather than representing the ordinary finger-related verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Self-magnification, pride, haughtiness, or insolent vain glory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A toe, as a digit of the foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a broader Classical Arabic bodily-part use distinct from the Quranic occurrences, which refer to fingers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A good visible impress or favorable effect, especially the mark of good care on livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may also describe a good effect or favor upon a person or property, including an effect attributed to God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression بِهِمْ تُثْنَى الأَصَابِعُ, to be counted among the best or among the select.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional idiom in which the fingers are figuratively bent when such people are mentioned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unfaithful, treacherous, or perfidious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the fixed figurative expression مُغِلُّ الإِصْبَعِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have a hand or involvement in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression using the finger as a sign of participation or influence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression قَلْبُ المُؤْمِنِ بَيْنَ إِصْبَعَيْنِ مِنْ أَصَابِعِ اللَّهِ, a figurative image of the believer's heart being under God's turning and control.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional theological expression, not a literal bodily description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To accomplish or dispose of an affair with extreme ease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer even to accomplishing it with one's smallest finger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A byname of the Devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional proper epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prong or projection resembling a finger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or technical extension based on shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Common clinopodium or wild basil, a sweet-smelling plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical name based on the resemblance of the plant to fingers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of long black grapes, likened to the dyed fingers of virgins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional botanical or agricultural name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flowers of the plant called سُورَنْجَان.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical name for the flowers, associated with the medicinal plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Red objects resembling finger-length applicators, used medicinally to help consolidate wounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional medicinal designation based on their shape and appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hand-shaped root of a plant with yellow and white variegation, used medicinally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported uses include treatment for madness or diabolical possession, poisons, venomous bites, and thick excrescences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A finger-breadth used as a unit of measure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Defined as the width of six moderate-sized barleycorns, or one quarter of a قبضَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Self-magnifying or proud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative derived form describing a person characterized by pride or self-exaltation.

lane_unit_coverage.note: A Form IV livestock-management gloss is reported, but the entry explicitly suggests it may result from a mistranscription of a noun expression.
Dialectal/orthographic substitution of ع for ح in a variant equated with صُبْحٌ.
Pointer-only entry referring back to the primary finger definition.
Pointer-only entry referring back to صَبْعٌ.

cautions: The public headword is the normalized singular citation form إِصْبَعٌ; the two supplied Quran occurrences are its plural form أَصَابِعَ.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane Form IV entry اصبع reports a livestock-management meaning but explicitly suggests that the report may derive from a mistranscription of لِلرَّاعِي عَلَى مَاشِيَتِهِ إِصْبَعٌ; it is therefore left unresolved rather than presented as an established Form IV lexical sense.
